pillar_reactions.evidence: Asked to start rather than to understand: 'what questions do have on the training and mobility side of things? Um, when do we start?' The mobility framing was aimed squarely at his stated goal — the rep offered a personal proof point, 'when I first started doing the mobility stuff that Trevor gave me, I had a bunch of shoulder issues. My ankle was kind of messed up within like, four weeks, like pretty much gone' — and it landed without a single question.

'Not necessarily. mean, it sounds like it'll be more of kind of, you know, general guidelines, which is fine.' The pitch was pre-framed to his existing one-meal-a-day pattern — 'I don't actually think it's bad that you're just eating one meal a day' — and to his dislike of tracking, so there was nothing left to push back on.

'Okay, good. Sweet.' Flat delivery relative to the fact that he had himself named accountability as the single reason coaching would help. The eight-kilogram guarantee was delivered inside this pillar and drew no reaction or question at all.

anchors.raw: I can research stuff online all day, every day, and everybody says this, this guy says that, and, you know, I do some of these workouts from some people, and I'm like, these are, yeah, I don't, yeah, that's not really doing a whole lot.
anchors.competitor: Free online kettlebell content, including Trevor's own
anchors.note: He has been running Trevor's free workouts for a couple of months, five days a week — 'the workouts that I followed that Trevor's done online, I actually feel like I'm working out the entire time'. The free version of the product is what brought him in and is what he is currently satisfied with; the paid programme has to be worth $6,000 more than something he already has. It never surfaced as price resistance, but it is the number in the room.

anchors.raw: I did start doing a TRT a few months back and that's kind of coincided with the energy levels.
anchors.note: He is already paying for an ongoing clinical intervention and attributes a real result to it, which establishes both a willingness to spend on his own health and a precedent that paid interventions work. The rep noticed the opening and used it — 'I know the TRT obviously helped a lot with energy, but I think like once we really start getting the nutrition side of things dialed in as well, you'll notice like a very significant increase in your energy.'

anchors.raw: I invest a lot in precious metals and whatnot.
anchors.note: Not a price anchor in the usual sense but the same function: the $6,000 has to clear a physical-gold sale at a shop in the next town before it exists. Net worth was never the constraint; liquidity is. No financial picture was taken, so nothing about his actual capacity to pay is on record.

unmet_demand.want: A credible answer on whether eating one meal a day is harmful — he raised the disagreement himself: 'my father's convinced that that's a bad thing, and I'm not entirely sure'.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He got a coach's personal opinion and habit rather than an assessment: 'I don't actually think it's bad that you're just eating one meal a day... Like I'll tend to fast until the evening.' The stated concern was narrowed to protein and calorie baselines, and the underlying question — is this pattern safe for a 38-year-old on testosterone replacement sleeping five to six hours — was never addressed by anyone qualified to address it.
